Seclusion

/sih-KLOO-zhuhn/ - the stress falls on KLOO · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Seclusion means the state of being hidden away or apart from others.

The treaty talks were held in strict seclusion at a mountain lodge, its gates closed to reporters for the week.

Worked Example

After the king's death, custom required the queen to pass a year in seclusion. She kept to the east wing, received no callers, and appeared exactly twice — a veiled figure at her window during the two great festivals. Courtiers argued over whether the seclusion was grief or statecraft; either way, no one saw her to ask.

Seclusion is the precise word because it names the state of being hidden from others — nothing about her feelings, only her apartness. Loneliness would claim she suffered; privacy would be far too weak for a year behind one wing's doors.

How Seclusion Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

solitude

solitude: the state of being alone, without the note of being hidden

privacy

privacy: control over what others may see or know — much weaker

Antonyms

company

company: the presence of other people

limelight

limelight: the glare of public attention

How Strong Is It? — privacy → solitude → seclusion

privacy vs. seclusion

privacy vs. seclusion: Privacy only fences off parts of your life while you live among others; seclusion withdraws the whole person from view.

solitude vs. seclusion

solitude vs. seclusion: Solitude means being alone, perhaps just for an afternoon walk; seclusion goes further — hidden away, out of reach, often behind real walls or miles.

Sort It Out

Now place each word on the right side of seclusion.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — se-

Prefix — se-: apart, away

Root — clus

Root — clus: to shut (Latin claudere, clusus)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: state of

Put it together

Put it together: Se- (apart) + clus (to shut) + -ion (state of) = the state of being shut apart. Latin claudere, 'to shut,' powers a whole family of closing words; add se-, 'away,' and you get seclusion — the door shut with you on the quiet side of it.

Use the root in a new word: exclude

Use the root in a new word: exclude: The tasting menu excludes anyone with a shellfish allergy, so the chef keeps an alternate list.

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Seclusion is usually chosen and can be restful — a writer's cabin, closed-door talks. You met isolation among this unit's words: that is the imposed cousin, cut off by blizzard, distance, or quarantine rather than by choice. And where alienation is a feeling that follows you into a crowd, seclusion is a matter of fact: hidden away, out of sight.
